prompt: Implement k-nearest-neighbour classification with Euclidean distance over a tiny fixed dataset, including the tie-break rule. Complete the distance and classify methods in the starter file.
explanation: k-NN has no training phase at all: it measures the distance from the query to every stored example, keeps the k closest, and lets them vote. Sorting an array of indexes rather than the points themselves keeps every distance paired with its label. The tie-break then falls out for free -- walk the neighbours in distance order and return the first label that reaches the winning count, because the closest of the tied labels is always the one you meet first.
hints: Compute all the distances once into an array, then sort an array of indexes with a comparator that looks those distances up.
A Map<String, Integer> counts the labels among the first k neighbours; getOrDefault keeps the increment to one line.
Find the highest count first, then scan the neighbours again in distance order and return the first label whose count matches it.
